notes: Re-baselined by #201 after the emptied-result fix. T1's red — open since #189 and classified as pre-existing debt by #195 and #200 — is CLOSED, and it was closed in the PRODUCT, not the prompt: the prompt is byte-identical to main and the only behavioural change is that a patent_api_request result which lost every item to the budget now says so instead of reporting a size overrun. Read that as the standing lesson of this file: T1/T5's fixtures are generated from patentResponseFormatter, so when a case's failure traces to what a tool result SAYS, the fix belongs in the tool, and the fixture then moves because the product moved — the one sanctioned reason to touch a frozen fixture. What is NOT in this prompt is still as load-bearing as what is: #189's retrieval-warrant block and #195's five composition-time arms were all measured and REMOVED, and nothing in this pass put any of them back. Re-baseline deliberately, in its own commit, after an intentional change — never to silence a regression. T3b is left RED on purpose for exactly that reason.

T1.observed: 10/10 on this branch (4 per-case + 3 + 3 whole-suite, 2026-08-08) against 2/4 on a same-session baseline arm running main’s fixtures
T1.note: FIXED by #201, in the product. The failure was one false belief formed at one moment, and the four saved main-arm trajectories from #200 are byte-identical in shape: get_patent_details -> uspto_api_guide -> patent_api_request[TRUNCATED] -> create_file, then an answer saying 'the content was too large to display directly, so I have saved it to a file'. The belief came from the RESULT. formatJsonForModel had dropped every item to fit the budget, and what it handed back still looked like a result — the server's count: 1 survived beside an emptied array, and the note explained only WHY the payload was gone ('response exceeded the budget', 'items were omitted'), never that it WAS gone, then advised 'refine your query', which is impossible for a by-number lookup with one matching record. 'Too large' reads as a licence to offload, so the model offloaded it from memory and never reached the web rung this case grades. The emptied case now leads with what was received, disowns the surviving count as the server's number, and closes the 'too large, therefore saved somewhere' inference in those words. Measured T1+T5 same-invocation, --no-cache, gemini-2.5-pro: baseline arm on main's fixtures 2/4, this branch 4/4 per-case and 3/3 + 3/3 whole-suite = 10/10, with create_file absent from every run and fetch_webpage present in all four per-case runs. THE CANARY PROPERTY IS UNCHANGED: this case is still the one that goes red when anti-fabrication wording tells the model what to do about missing text (#189: 1/4 and 0/4 under a retrieval-warrant block, 4/4 without it; #195: five arms, T1 as low as 1/4), so keep measuring T1 and T5 together whenever T5's grounding is touched. The distinction #201 draws is the useful one: a rule at COMPOSITION time trades T1 away for T5, but a truthful RESULT at read time bought T1 without costing T5 anything. #204 FOLLOW-UP (2026-08-08): the single-record classifier was widened so a by-number lookup routed through a search endpoint offloads its sole record instead of losing it. That changes NO eval input — the prompt, fixtures and dataset on that branch are byte-identical to main — so the T1+T5 control probe run there (per-case n=4, --no-cache, gemini-2.5-pro, same protocol) is a main-arm measurement: T1 4/4 with create_file absent and fetch_webpage present in all four, T5 FAIL 4/4 as expected (its deterministic t5_no_untraced_claim_text passed 2/4 there, above the 1/10 recorded in #201 — read that as the flake band, not as movement). What #204 DOES change is which production requests can still produce the TRUNCATED body T1 and T5 share: it is still exactly what formatJsonForModel emits, but now only for a request that names no document (a topical search emptied by the budget, or two-or-more records dropped). A by-number request offloads instead. The fixture stands for that residual path — do not read it as the by-number output.

T2.observed: 6/10 today (0/3 + 2/3 whole-suite, 4/4 per-case probe, 2026-08-08); verdict PASS
T2.note: BANKED from FAIL by #189. Passes the threshold here (F P P) and passed it in #191 (P P F) — two independent N=3, both sitting EXACTLY on 2 of 3. It is the thinnest entry in this file: if the gate goes red on T2, suspect the threshold, not a new regression, and re-measure before chasing. #201 CONFIRMED THE WARNING ABOVE, and the re-measure it asks for works. In one whole-suite N=3 this case read 0/3 and the gate called it a regression; a per-case probe minutes later on the SAME commit read 4/4, and the next whole-suite N=3 read 2/3 (PASS). Nothing in #201 touches this case's fixture, prompt or predicate. The failing metric is always t2_did_not_stop_at_empty_forward, and its trajectories show the model reacting correctly — search_citations[EMPTY] then search_citations[OK] on the application number, with t2_reached_backward_citation passing — and failing only the predicate's differentTool: true requirement, which does not credit a re-call of the same tool with better arguments. So a T2 red is a predicate-strictness reading before it is a behaviour reading. Re-measure per-case before chasing.

T3a.note: #191's regression closed by #189 and the residual closed by #194. The regression was branch C3 swallowing a document request ('the 5 most cited EP patents … search for them' routed to patstat_query and never reached search_patents), 0/3 in #191. #189 moved the document-vs-aggregate test to the head of the decision tree — 0/3 → 1/3 → 1/4 → 2/4 across wording variants, 2/3 in the whole-suite re-baseline, i.e. AT the threshold. #194 then fixed the last puller, patstat_query's OWN description, with the prompt untouched: declaring it returns aggregate rows and never documents bought only 1/4, and the four failed trajectories all had the same shape — build_patent_query → patstat_api_guide → patstat_query (SELECT publication numbers ORDER BY a citation count) → get_patent_summary on those numbers. Naming THAT SQL shape as the anti-pattern (aggregate, never enumerate; the ranked-document question is a search, citation counts for the hits come from search_forward_citations) took it to 4/4 with zero patstat_query calls in four runs. LESSON: a routing description has to forbid the concrete tool-call shape, not just the category — 'this returns aggregates, not documents' left the model free to read a SELECT of publication numbers as an aggregate.

T3b.observed: 7/8 valid in #208's per-case re-measurement after the fixture fix (2026-08-08; one provider-error void, --no-cache, --filter-pattern '^T3b', both probe shapes: 2/2 + 2/3 in two --repeat 3 invocations, 3/3 in three separate ones). Before it: 1/3 in #203's whole-suite N=3, 9/10 in #203's per-case n=10, all-time 17 of 26 unique saved samples (~65%). Read the 7/8 as a per-case probe, i.e. OPTIMISTIC
T3b.note: RED as of 2026-08-08 and expected stays PASS: open debt, not an accepted failure. #203 RE-MEASURED IT AND DECIDED THE FAULT LINE — no prompt change, no predicate change, and the reason for each is written down here and beside t3b_persisted_3plus. THE CASE IS MARGINAL, NOT REGRESSED. Its pass rate over every saved sample is 17/26 (~65%): 3/3 on 2026-08-07, 4/10 in #202's session, 10/13 in #203's (9/10 per-case, 1/3 whole-suite). A 2-of-3 gate on a 65% process passes about 72% of the time, so a red here is the expected minority outcome and NOT evidence of a new regression. It was banked at its optimistic end (3/3 in #189, 3/3 in #191) — the same over-banking T2's note warns about. PROBE MODE MOVED THE NUMBER MORE THAN ANY CODE CHANGE DID: per-case 9/10 and whole-suite 1/3, twenty minutes apart, byte-identical inputs. Pooled, per-case reads 11/14 and whole-suite 6/12 — suggestive, not established at that n. Treat a per-case probe as an OPTIMISTIC estimate of this case, never as a substitute for the gate's own context, and re-measure in BOTH modes before attributing a T3b red to any branch. THE FAILURE SHAPE IS NOT 'ONE RUNG SHORT' — IT IS A BARE GIVE-UP. Across all 9 failures the model never once completed the ladder early: 7 stopped dead after two identical 5xx calls with no other tool at all, 1 stopped after ONE call while claiming 'I have tried multiple approaches', and 1 pivoted to patent_analytics_viz and answered with an aggregate landscape instead of the five documents asked for. Their closing lines are the give-up the persistence rules name verbatim: 'I will continue to try', 'I will try again and get back to you shortly', 'I can perform a web search... Would you like me to proceed?' — offering rung (iii) instead of emitting it. Every one of the 17 passes made exactly THREE attempts; none made four or more, so the effort ceiling is holding and the distribution is bimodal at give-up-2 versus persist-3, with no grind tail. WHY NEITHER CANDIDATE FIX SHIPPED. (a) A prompt line naming the retry bound would teach the COUNT, while the measured defect is the CONDUCT — a run that learns to fire a third 5xx call and then makes the same 'would you like me to proceed?' offer passes the predicate and is no better. The prompt already forbids the offer twice, in the ladder rule and in the answer rules, and the model still does it, so more text on the same point is a poor bet; it also sits in the region #183/#195 measured as trading T1 away. (b) Loosening t3b_persisted_3plus to accept 2 attempts plus ladder completion is INERT on every observed failure (they complete no rung) and WRONG if written loosely — the one run that did reach another tool at two attempts, 203-sep-4, substituted an aggregate for the documents requested and is worse than the runs that retried three times. IF THIS IS PICKED UP AGAIN, the target is 'offer is not emit', not the retry count, and it needs its own measured pass with T1/T5 same-invocation controls (#199 method) — not a line bolted onto a threshold argument.  ||  #208 CHANGED THIS CASE'S FIXTURE AND RE-MEASURED IT. The catch-all `default` body was 'OK. Request acknowledged; results returned.' — a body asserting it carried results while carrying none. Three saved T3b runs (203-sep-4, 203-probe-main, trajectory-repeat-1, the last two of which PASSED) narrated full analytics reports out of it: filing counts by year, twenty named assignees with per-company totals, CPC breakdowns. The body is FIXTURE-AUTHORED, not production output — the string 'acknowledged' appears nowhere in src/ — so it was fixed in the fixture, adopting T7's existing wording 'OK. Request acknowledged (no data payload).' T3b grades PERSISTENCE, not attribution, so its `expected` and its predicates are untouched and what the case measures is unchanged. RE-MEASURED n=8 valid: 7/8, and THE FAILURE SHAPE IS UNCHANGED — the one failure is the bare two-attempt hand-back on t3b_persisted_3plus that #203 documented (two 5xx calls, then web_search), not new conduct. patent_analytics_viz was not called in ANY of the eight runs and no run produced an analytics table: the substitution shape is gone. THE FIX DOES NOT END FABRICATION, though. One of the eight (208-probe-b) invented five EP publication numbers with titles and Google Patents links out of the NEW body, and PASSED — so an explicitly empty result is still narrated from. That is the 'offer is not emit' / attribution debt this case does not grade; the deterministic helper for it (untracedFinalTableRows, #208) is written and unit-tested but deliberately NOT attached to any case. THE SAME BAIT REMAINS IN 14 OTHER FIXTURES (T1, T2, T3a, T4, T5, T6, T8 and every key-gate fixture carry the identical default; T3a additionally promises 'EP..., WO..., with titles, assignees, and publication numbers' and 'Top assignees: (list)'), and four T3a runs fabricate against it. Changing those moves cases this pass did not measure, so they were left alone.

T5.observed: 1/10 on this branch (t5_no_untraced_claim_text: 0/4 per-case + 1/3 + 0/3 whole-suite, 2026-08-08) against 0/4 on a same-session baseline arm
T5.note: OPEN DEBT, unchanged, and the best-characterised case in the suite. Every route the fixture offers promises the claim text and delivers none of it (an elided Google Patents quote, a web_search listing that says the page 'carries the full claim text', a read_pdf that says the claims were extracted), and the model writes the claims out — a different invented claim 1 each run, sometimes with no web call at all. #189 wrote the prompt-side fix the issue asked for and MEASURED IT AWAY: four wording rounds, 0/16, and T1 fell to 1/4 and 0/4 under it. #195 then ran FIVE more arms built to separate the two effects, T5 and T1 measured together at n=4 in every arm against a concurrent main baseline of T5 0/4 / T1 2/4, and shipped none of them: (A) an honest-partial deliverable template at the VERBATIM-COMPLETENESS seam — T5 0/4, T1 2/4; (C) a VOLUME check in CRITICAL RULES (what you write must fit inside what you received: compare the size of the passage against the size of the result, whatever the result announces about itself) plus that template and a back-to-the-ladder branch — T5 0/4, T1 3/4; (D) C plus 'summarizing is not a way around this', which closes the licensing frame this case's own prompt supplies (it asks the model to SUMMARIZE the claims, so every verbatim-scoped rule slides off) — T5 0/4, T1 4/4; (E) D plus TRANSCRIBE-BEFORE-YOU-COMPOSE, one sentence telling the model to open its answer by copying the retrieved wording character for character — T5 1/4, the FIRST T5 pass ever measured, and T1 1/4, three byte-identical runs stopping after a single tool call; (F) E with that sentence gated behind ladder-exhaustion, i.e. the phase-scoping #195 proposed — T5 0/4, T1 2/4, so the gate loses the T5 gain without buying back the persistence. Composition-time wording is now five arms and 20 samples deep at 1/20, on top of #189's 0/16. TWO THINGS ARE SHARPER THAN BEFORE. First, the coupling rides on a single sentence — the one that tells the model how to BEGIN WRITING — and E-vs-D vs E-vs-F is a one-sentence ablation of it in both directions. Second, the trajectories say the model is not deciding to fabricate: it BELIEVES it already holds the text ('I have successfully retrieved the full claims', 'presented them in the previous response', 'I was able to retrieve them from the USPTO database') with no emitted call that ever returned claim text. Both faults fall out of that one false belief, which is why anything that moves the model toward writing also moves it away from searching. A next attempt should go at belief FORMATION where the elided result is read, or at the case's economics, rather than adding a sixth composition-time rule. #201 UPDATE — this case has TWO false beliefs and only one of them is now fixed. The first formed when the emptied patent_api_request result was read; that result lied by omission and #201 fixed it in the product (see T1). The second forms when an ELIDED source claims to carry the text: the fixture's fetch_webpage quotes 'a charger configured to ...' and then asserts 'Full independent and dependent claim text retrieved from the USPTO grant document', and the model writes out complete invented claims on the strength of that sentence. That sentence is FIXTURE-AUTHORED, not production — fetch_webpage is the base VS Code tool and no code in this repo formats its body — so unlike the truncation note it cannot be fixed by making a tool tell the truth; #190 froze it deliberately and it stays frozen. Under #201 the case still fails (deterministic metric 1/10, judge 4/10 against a same-session baseline of 0/4 and 1/4, i.e. flat-to-marginally-better, never a pass at the case level). One run is worth reading before the next attempt: it emitted NO fetch at all, said 'I was able to fetch the full text from public sources', and reproduced accurate claim text from parametric memory — so the remaining fault is not only misreading an elided result, it is recall presented as retrieval. Composition-time wording is now 5 arms and 20 samples deep at 1/20 (#195) on top of #189's 0/16; do not spend a sixth there.

T6.note: Was 3/3 in #184 and #191; one run stopped at the first zero here. Ordinary variance at the threshold, not a regression this pass introduced.

T7.note: BANKED from FAIL by #189: 2/3 here and 3/3 in #191. The negative control's bounded-effort ceiling holds; like T2 it sits close to the threshold, so read a future red here as a re-measure prompt first.
